questions.problem:
The number of cells in a petri dish $C(t)$ after $t$ hours can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}=C.
$$

If there are currently $650$ cells in the petri dish, calculate the number of cells after $2$ hours. Round your answer to the nearest integer.

The number of cells after $2$ hours is approximately 
{{field-1}}
cells.
questions.worked_solution:
We model the number of cells using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}C}{\text{d}t}=C.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
C(t)={C}_{0}\,{e}^{t},
$$

where ${C}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that there are currently $650$ cells in the petri dish, so we have ${C}_{0}=650.$

Therefore, the number of cells $C$ at time $t$ is

$$
C(t)=650\,{e}^{t}.
$$

Finally, to find the number of cells when $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}C(2) & =650\,{e}^{2} \\  & ≈4802.89\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that the number of cells after $2$ hours is approximately $4803$ cells.

questions.problem:
The value of a savings account $A=A(t)$ after $t$ years can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=kA,
$$

where $k>0$ is the growth rate. If the account initially had $$12\,000,$ and $A(4)=$15\,000,$ calculate the growth rate $k$ to the nearest percent.
questions.worked_solution:
We model the value of the savings account using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=kA.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
A(t)={A}_{0}\,{e}^{kt},
$$

where ${A}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that the account initially had $$12\,000,$ so we have ${A}_{0}=12\,000.$

Therefore, the value $A$ at time $t$ is

$$
A(t)=12\,000\,{e}^{kt}.
$$

Finally, to find the value of $k,$ we substitute $A(4)=15\,000$ into the equation above and solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A(4) & =12\,000\,{e}^{k\cdot 4} \\ 15\,000 & =12\,000\,{e}^{4k} \\ {e}^{4k} & =\frac{15\,000}{12\,000} \\ {e}^{4k} & =1.25 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4k}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.25) \\ 4k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.25) \\ k & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.25) \\ k & =0.055\,78…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k≈6%,$ rounded to the nearest percent.

canonical_examples.problem:
Suppose that the population $P(t)$ of a town after $t$ years can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\dfrac {\textrm{d}P} {\textrm{d}t} = 0.02P.
$$

If there are currently $500$ people in the town, what will be the town's population in $3$ years?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We note that this is an exponential growth differential equation with $r = 0.02$. Therefore, the solution to this equation is

$$
P(t) = P_0\,e^{0.02t},
$$

where $P_0$ is the initial value.

We're told that the population is currently $500,$ so we have $P_0 = 500.$ 

Therefore, the population of the town at time $t$ is

$$
P(t) = 500\,e^{0.02t}.
$$

Finally, to find the population after $3$ years, we substitute $t=3$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3) & =500\,{e}^{0.02\cdot 3} \\  & =500\,{e}^{0.06} \\  & ≈531\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the population will be approximately $531$ after $3$ years.

canonical_examples.problem:
Suppose that the value $V(t)$ of a particular car can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d V}{\textrm d t} = -0.1V,
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the car was first purchased. If the car was purchased for $\[math]10\,000,$ what will it be worth after $3$ years?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that the right-hand side of the equation is *negative*, which means that the car's value is *decreasing.*

This is an exponential decay differential equation with $r = 0.1.$ Therefore, the general solution to this equation is

$$
V(t) = V_0 e^{-0.1 t}.
$$

We know that the car was first purchased for $\[math]10\,000.$ Therefore, $V_0 = 10\,000,$ and we have the particular solution

$$
V(t) = 10\,000 e^{-0.1 t}.
$$

To find the car's value after $3$ years, we substitute $t=3$ into the particular solution above. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}V(3) & =10\,000{e}^{-0.1\cdot 3} \\  & =10\,000{e}^{-0.3} \\  & ≈7\,408.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the car will be worth approximately $\[/math]7\,408$ after three years.

canonical_examples.problem: The number of followers of a celebrity's social media account increases at a rate that is directly proportional to the number of followers at that time. Given that there are currently $600\,000$ followers and in $3$ months there will be $780\,000$ followers, what is the growth rate? Round your answer to the nearest percent.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The rate $N'(t)$ at which the number of followers increases is directly proportional to the number of followers $N.$ Therefore, we can model the number of followers using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} N}{\mathrm{d} t} = rN,
$$

where $t$ is measured in months, and $r > 0$ is the growth rate.

The solution to this equation is

$$
N(t) = N_0\,e^{rt},
$$

where $N_0$ is the initial number of followers.

We're told that there are currently $600\,000$ followers, so we have $N_0 = 600\,000.$

Therefore, the number of followers $N$ after $t$ months is

$$
N(t) = 600\,000 \, e^{rt} .
$$

Finally, to find the growth rate, we substitute $N(3)=780\,000$ into the equation above and solve for $r,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(3) & =600\,000\,{e}^{r\cdot 3} \\ 780\,000 & =600\,000\,{e}^{3r} \\ {e}^{3r} & =\frac{780\,000}{600\,000} \\ {e}^{3r} & =1.3 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3r}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.3) \\ 3r & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.3) \\ r & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.3) \\ r & ≈0.087\,54\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $r\approx 9\%,$ rounded to the nearest percent.
